This is a safe, sensible plan, and it answers Nessa's question directly. The answer is a clear no to adding the missed runs, and it doesn't even put back the third run. That fits someone coming off a 38.4 fever who still has a cough and feels wiped out. Next week has only two short 24-minute walk-runs, on Wednesday and Saturday. Each one is conditional on no fever and normal breathing. Rest days around them give the cold time to clear. Volume comes in a little under her recent 6.8–7.3 km weeks, so the plan backs off for her tiredness and doesn't rush her back. Every day can be run as written.

Weaknesses:
- The safety flag says "fever… still lingering," but she hasn't had a fever since Friday. That's a small misreading of the card.
- "Your Monday run went as planned" assumes which day she ran. It's a reasonable guess, since she fell ill on Tuesday, but the card doesn't say.
- The heart-rate cap assumes she has a monitor.
- It doesn't tell her to see a GP if the cough lingers or moves to her chest.
- What we can see doesn't reassure her about the 15 November 5K.
These are small points. None of them makes the plan unsafe.

shown:
── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Skipping the two missed runs was the right call while you were ill, and your Monday run went as planned. …
Answers: No, the plan does not add the two missed runs and it does not add a third run this week. Next week has two short run-walks, Wednesday and Saturday, and each one only if you have no fever and your breathing feels normal.
Safety flag: Fever and cough still lingering
Next week:
Mon: rest, no running. Walking the dog at an easy pace is fine if you feel up to it…
Tue: other, 20 min easy walk. Keep the pace relaxed enough to talk. This gets you moving…
Wed: easy, 24 min walk-run, 8 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, heart rate under 145. Run only…
Thu: rest. Two rest days in a row give the cold time to clear before the next run.
Fri: rest. Keep the day fully easy so the legs and chest recover fully before Saturday.
Sat: easy, 24 min walk-run, 8 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, heart rate under 145. Same…
Sun: rest. Let the week settle. A relaxed walk with the dog is fine if you feel well.
